## Code Review: `inspect` logical-node view and `--containers` flag

### ScopeThe PR reworks `clab inspect` listing in `cmd/inspect.go`:

- A new `--containers` flag (`o.Inspect.Containers`) is wired through `cmd/options.go` and documented in `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md`.
- `listContainers` now always lists by containerlab labels (lab name, or the bare `containerlab` label for `--all`) and, in `--topo` mode, merges in topology-node containers that have no labels (ext-containers).
- A new `logicalNodeContainers` function collapses the container list into one logical entry per topology node: tool containers are hidden, internal netns holders are hidden but their network settings (mgmt IP) are copied onto the logical node, and for distributed SR-SIM only the CPM component (`<root>-a`, falling back to `<root>-b` when CPM A is absent) represents the chassis.
- The per-container internal filter inside `PrintContainerInspect` is removed; `--details` now returns every container of a lab.
- A new unit test `TestLogicalNodeContainers` covers the grouping logic.

### Summary table

| Priority | Count | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 1 | Stale evergreen doc contradicts new `inspect` behavior for internal containers |
| P4 | 2 | `--topo` label listing can surface same-name labs' containers; `--details` silently adopts the per-container view without documentation |

### Findings

#### P3 — Stale claim in `docs/manual/kinds/srl.md`: internal container "only listed by `inspect --all`"

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L214–L219](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L214-L219) (introducing change) — counterpart: [`docs/manual/kinds/srl.md` L473](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md#L473)

**Problem:** The PR removes the `!o.Destroy.All` internal-container filter, so `inspect --all` no longer lists internal containers at all; they are now shown only via `--containers` (and `--details`). However, the evergreen kind documentation still states: "The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node." (A published release note, `docs/rn/0.80.md` line 250, makes the same claim but is immutable per the repository's release-note rule and should not be edited.)

**Trigger:** Any user reading the SR Linux "Reboot" section and running `inspect --all` to find the `<node>-netns` holder.

**Impact:** The documented command no longer surfaces the internal container, so users following the doc cannot find the holder that carries the node's mgmt address and restart state.

**Correction:** Update the sentence in `docs/manual/kinds/srl.md` to say the internal container is hidden from the default logical view and listed with `containerlab inspect --containers` (or `--details`). No other kind docs make this claim (checked `docs/manual/kinds/*`).

#### P4 — `inspect --topo` now lists every container sharing the lab name, not only the topology's own nodes

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L184–L196](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L184-L196)

**Problem:** In the `--topo` branch, `listContainers` now lists all containers whose `containerlab` label equals `c.Config.Name`, where base listed only the topology's node containers via `ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound`. Containerlab does not enforce lab-name uniqueness across directories, so a second lab deployed from a different directory with the same name contributes containers that `logicalNodeContainers` cannot distinguish (same `containerlab` label) and will render as logical nodes of the inspected lab.

**Trigger:** `clab inspect -t <topo>` while a different lab with the same lab name (disjoint node names) is running.

**Impact:** The topo-scoped view can show rows belonging to an unrelated lab, including entries with a foreign `labPath`. Low likelihood, but a silent output widening relative to the merge base; the same widening does not apply to the `--name` branch, which already had this semantics at base.

**Correction:** Optionally scope the `--topo` label listing with the topology path label (`clab-topo-file`, set on every node config in `core/config.go` and inherited by components and holders), e.g. by adding an equality filter through the existing `clabcore.WithListFilter` option; ext-containers without labels are still covered by the `ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound` merge. If the widening is considered acceptable, at least note in the docs that `--topo` lists by lab name.

#### P4 — `--details` implicitly switches to the per-container view, undocumented

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L214–L217](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L214-L217) — missing counterpart: the `#### details` section of [`docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` L64–L68](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md#L64-L68)

**Problem:** `listContainers` returns the raw container list whenever `o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details`, so `--details` now includes internal netns holders, tool containers (sshx, gotty, …) and SR-SIM line-card components. The new `#### containers` docs section explains the per-container view, but the `#### details` section still only says it outputs "every bit of information about the running containers" without stating that it implies the `--containers` view. Notably, for netns-based nodes the management IP moves to the internal `<node>-netns` entry (a node container sharing another container's netns has no IP of its own); at base, `--topo --details` reported the merged IP on the node entry. The new behavior is consistent across `--name`/`--topo` (at base, `--name --details` was already unmerged), so this is a documentation gap rather than a defect.

**Trigger:** `clab inspect --details` on a lab with SR Linux/SR-SIM nodes or tool containers.

**Impact:** Scripts consuming the `--details` JSON for `ipv4_address`/`ipv6_address` of netns-based nodes now find those fields empty on the node entry and populated on the internal holder entry; the docs do not prepare them for this.

**Correction:** Add one sentence to the `#### details` section stating that it lists every container (equivalent to `--containers`) rather than one logical entry per node.

173: func listContainers(
174: 	ctx context.Context,
175: 	c *clabcore.CLab,
176: 	o *Options,
177: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
178: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
179: 		return c.ListLabRuntimeContainers(ctx, o.Destroy.All)
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	var listOptions []clabcore.ListOption
183: 
184: 	switch {
185: 	case o.Global.TopologyFile != "":
186: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
187: 	case o.Global.TopologyName != "":
188: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListLabName(o.Global.TopologyName))
189: 	default:
190: 		listOptions = append(listOptions, clabcore.WithListclabLabelExists())
191: 	}
192: 
193: 	containers, err := c.ListContainers(ctx, listOptions...)
194: 	if err != nil {
195: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list containers based on labels: %s", err)
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	// containers that containerlab did not create (ie. ext-container) have no lab labels.
199: 	if o.Global.TopologyFile != "" {
200: 		nodeContainers, err := c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
201: 		if err != nil {

203: 		}

205: 		for idx := range nodeContainers {

207: 				return ctr.ID == nodeContainers[idx].ID
208: 			}) {
209: 				containers = append(containers, nodeContainers[idx])
210: 			}
211: 		}

214: 	// --details always describes every container of a lab.
215: 	if o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details {

219: 	return logicalNodeContainers(containers), nil

222: // logicalNodeContainers returns a single logical topology node
223: func logicalNodeContainers(
224: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
225: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
226: 	// Node names are unique only within a lab.
227: 	type nodeKey struct{ lab, node string }
228: 
229: 	holders := make(map[nodeKey]*clabruntime.GenericContainer)
230: 	hasCPMA := make(map[nodeKey]bool)
231: 
232: 	for idx := range containers {
233: 		l := containers[idx].Labels
234: 		key := nodeKey{l[clabconstants.Containerlab], l[clabconstants.RootNodeName]}
235: 
236: 		switch {
237: 		case key.node == "":
238: 		case l[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true":
239: 			holders[key] = &containers[idx]
240: 		case l[clabconstants.NodeName] == key.node+"-a":
241: 			hasCPMA[key] = true
242: 		}
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	result := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(containers))
246: 
247: 	for idx := range containers {
248: 		ctr := containers[idx]
249: 		name := ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]
250: 		key := nodeKey{ctr.Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab], ctr.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName]}
251: 
252: 		// Components are named <root node>-<lowercase slot>.
253: 		isCPM := name == key.node+"-a" || (name == key.node+"-b" && !hasCPMA[key])
254: 		if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] != "" ||
255: 			ctr.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true" || (key.node != "" && !isCPM) {
256: 			continue
257: 		}
258: 
259: 		if key.node == "" {
260: 			key.node = name
261: 		}
262: 
263: 		if holder := holders[key]; holder != nil {
264: 			ctr.NetworkName = holder.NetworkName
265: 			ctr.NetworkSettings = holder.NetworkSettings
266: 			ctr.Ports = holder.Ports
267: 		}
268: 
269: 		result = append(result, ctr)
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	return result
273: }

588: // parseStatus extracts a simpler status string, focusing on health states.
589: func parseStatus(status string) string {
590: 	switch {
591: 	case strings.Contains(status, "unhealthy"):
592: 		return "unhealthy"
593: 	case strings.Contains(status, "health: starting"):
594: 		return "health: starting"
595: 	case strings.Contains(status, "healthy"):
596: 		return "healthy"
597: 	default:
598: 		// Return original status if no specific health info found
599: 		return status
600: 	}
601: }

603: // ipWithoutPrefix removes the CIDR prefix length from an IP address string.
604: // Returns "N/A" if input contains "N/A".
605: // Returns original string if it doesn't contain exactly one "/".
606: func ipWithoutPrefix(ip string) string {
607: 	if strings.Contains(ip, clabconstants.NotApplicable) {
608: 		return ip
609: 	}
610: 
611: 	ipParts := strings.Split(ip, "/")
612: 	if len(ipParts) != 2 { //nolint: mnd
613: 		return ip // Return original if not in expected format "address/prefix"
614: 	}
615: 
616: 	return ipParts[0]
617: }

```bash
containerlab tools netem set -n r1 -t netem.clab.yml -i eth1 --delay 5ms
containerlab tools netem show -t netem.clab.yml
```

Thanks @kaelemc #3409

## SR-SIM netns ownership

SR-SIM distributed chassis components are attached to an internal namespace pause container — the same way Kubernetes holds pod namespaces — so any component container can be killed and brought back without losing the network namespace. The internal container is hidden from `inspect` output unless `--all` is set.

Thanks @kaelemc #3397

## Fortinet FortiProxy

The new `fortinet_fortiproxy` kind aliases the [`fortinet_fortigate`](../manual/kinds/fortinet_fortigate.md) kind. For both kinds, the node's `license` file is now mounted into the vrnetlab container, where a TFTP server serves it to the VM for license activation.

Thanks @KarelChanivecky #3228

display.text:
```bash
containerlab tools netem set -n r1 -t netem.clab.yml -i eth1 --delay 5ms
containerlab tools netem show -t netem.clab.yml
```

Thanks @kaelemc #3409

## SR-SIM netns ownership

SR-SIM distributed chassis components are attached to an internal namespace pause container — the same way Kubernetes holds pod namespaces — so any component container can be killed and brought back without losing the network namespace. The internal container is hidden from `inspect` output unless `--all` is set.

Thanks @kaelemc #3397

## Fortinet FortiProxy

The new `fortinet_fortiproxy` kind aliases the [`fortinet_fortigate`](../manual/kinds/fortinet_fortigate.md) kind. For both kinds, the node's `license` file is now mounted into the vrnetlab container, where a TFTP server serves it to the VM for license activation.

Thanks @KarelChanivecky #3228

## Code Review: `clab inspect` logical-node view and the `--containers` flag

### Change summary

This PR reworks how `clab inspect` presents containers:

- A new `--containers` flag (`o.Inspect.Containers`) is registered in `cmd/inspect.go` and added to `InspectOptions` in `cmd/options.go`.
- `listContainers` is rewritten to always list by containerlab labels (lab name for `--topo`/`--name`, the bare `containerlab` label for `--all`), and — only in `--topo` mode — merges in topology-node containers that carry no labels (for example `ext-container`), deduplicated by container ID.
- A new `logicalNodeContainers` function collapses the container list into one logical entry per topology node: tool containers (sshx, gotty, …) are hidden, internal netns holders are hidden but their network settings (management IP) are copied onto the logical node, and for distributed SR-SIM only the CPM component (`<root>-a`, falling back to `<root>-b` when CPM A is absent) represents the chassis.
- The per-container internal filter inside `PrintContainerInspect` is removed; `--details` now returns every container of a lab.
- A new unit test `TestLogicalNodeContainers` covers the grouping logic, and the `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` page gains a `#### containers` section.

### Summary table

| Priority | Count | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | 0 | — |
| P1 | 0 | — |
| P2 | 0 | — |
| P3 | 1 | Stale evergreen doc contradicts the new `inspect` behavior for internal containers |
| P4 | 2 | `--topo` label listing can surface same-name labs' containers; `--details` silently adopts the per-container view without documentation |

### Findings

#### P3 — Stale claim in `docs/manual/kinds/srl.md`: internal container "only listed by `inspect --all`"

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L214–L217](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L214-L217) (introducing change) — missing counterpart: [`docs/manual/kinds/srl.md` L473](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/docs/manual/kinds/srl.md#L473)

**Problem:** The PR removes the `!o.Destroy.All` internal-container filtering from both `listContainers` and `PrintContainerInspect`, so `inspect --all` no longer lists internal containers at all; they are now shown only via `--containers` (and `--details`). The evergreen kind documentation still states verbatim: "The internal container is only listed by `containerlab inspect --all`, and it is removed together with the node." The same outdated wording appears in the published release note `docs/rn/0.80.md` line 250 ("hidden from `inspect` output unless `--all` is set"), but published release notes are immutable per the repository's release-note rule and must not be edited.

**Trigger:** Any user reading the SR Linux reboot documentation and running `inspect --all` to locate the `<node>-netns` holder.

**Impact:** The documented command no longer surfaces the internal container, so users following the documentation cannot find the holder that carries the node's management address and restart state.

**Correction:** Update the sentence in `docs/manual/kinds/srl.md` to say the internal container is hidden from the default logical view and listed with `containerlab inspect --containers` (or `--details`). No other kind page makes this claim (checked `docs/manual/kinds/*`).

#### P4 — `inspect --topo` now lists every container sharing the lab name, not only the topology's own nodes

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L184–L196](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L184-L196)

**Problem:** In the `--topo` branch, `listContainers` now lists all containers whose `containerlab` label equals `c.Config.Name`, where the merge base listed only the topology's node containers via `ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound`. Containerlab does not enforce lab-name uniqueness across directories, so a second lab deployed from a different directory with the same name contributes containers that `logicalNodeContainers` cannot distinguish (they share the same `containerlab` label) and will render as logical nodes of the inspected lab.

**Trigger:** Running `clab inspect -t <topo>` while a different lab with the same lab name (disjoint node names) is running on the same host.

**Impact:** The topo-scoped view can show rows belonging to an unrelated lab, including entries with a foreign lab path. This is low likelihood, but a silent output widening relative to the merge base. Note that the `--name` branch already had this label-based semantics at the merge base, so only the `--topo` path narrows in this review.

**Correction:** Optionally scope the `--topo` label listing with the topology path label (`clab-topo-file`, set on every node config in `core/config.go` L878 and inherited by components and holders), for example via the existing `clabcore.WithListFilter` option at `core/options_list.go` L178; ext-containers without labels remain covered by the `ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound` merge. If the widening is considered acceptable, at least note in the documentation that `--topo` lists by lab name.

#### P4 — `--details` implicitly switches to the per-container view, undocumented

**Location:** [`cmd/inspect.go` L214–L217](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/cmd/inspect.go#L214-L217) — missing counterpart: the `#### details` section of [`docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` L64–L68](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/b1d236f6f2dc493e7e2719bc6cdbcfff74ff8798/docs/cmd/inspect/index.md#L64-L68)

**Problem:** `listContainers` returns the raw container list whenever `o.Inspect.Containers || o.Inspect.Details`, so `--details` now includes internal netns holders, tool containers (sshx, gotty, …) and SR-SIM line-card components. The new `#### containers` section explains the per-container view, but the `#### details` section still only says it outputs "every bit of information about the running containers" without stating that it implies the `--containers` view. For netns-based nodes the management IP moves to the internal `<node>-netns` entry, since a container sharing another container's netns has no IP of its own; at the merge base, `--topo --details` reported the merged IP on the node entry, whereas `--name --details` was already unmerged. The new behavior is at least consistent across both selection modes, so this is a documentation gap rather than a defect.

**Trigger:** Running `clab inspect --details` on a lab with SR Linux/SR-SIM nodes or tool containers.

**Impact:** Scripts consuming the `--details` JSON for `ipv4_address`/`ipv6_address` of netns-based nodes now find those fields empty on the node entry and populated on the internal holder entry; the documentation does not prepare them for this.

**Correction:** Add one sentence to the `#### details` section of `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` stating that it lists every container (equivalent to `--containers`) rather than one logical entry per node.

### What was checked and found correct

- `logicalNodeContainers` correctness: traced against the real label scheme — SR Linux holders set `clab-internal-node: "true"`, `clab-root-node-name` and `NodeName: <node>-netns` (`nodes/srl/netns.go`), SR-SIM components set `RootNodeName` and are named `<root>-<lowercase slot>` by `calcComponentName` (`nodes/sros/sros.go`), and tool containers set `tool-type` (`cmd/tools.go`). The `hasCPMA`/CPM-B fallback mirrors `sros.cpmSlot()` (prefers A, falls back to B), including the cross-lab keying covered by the new test.
- The removed internal filter in `PrintContainerInspect` does not regress `clab deploy`: its only external caller (`cmd/deploy.go` L335) feeds `DeployResult.Containers` from `ListNodesContainers`, whose per-node `GetContainers` never returns holders for a healthy deploy (and a failed deploy aborts before printing, in `core/deploy.go`).
- The label-based listing works for both Docker and Podman (both populate `Labels` in `runtime/docker/docker.go` and `runtime/podman/util.go`).
- The c9s runtime path (`ListLabRuntimeContainers`) and `inspect interfaces` are untouched by the new filtering.
- The O(n²) dedup with `slices.ContainsFunc` is fine at lab scale (dozens of containers); no performance concern.
- Schema: no topology/schema-visible changes; the new flag is CLI-only, so `schemas/clab.schema.json` needs no edit.
- Docs: the new `#### containers` section accurately describes the default one-entry-per-node behavior and the `--containers` flag; the flag help text matches the implementation.

### Coverage notes

- Tests were not executed; this is a read-only snapshot with no test runner available. The new `TestLogicalNodeContainers` was verified by manual trace and matches the implementation for all its cases (tool skip, internal-without-root, SR Linux holder merge, CPM A/B fallback across two labs).
- All cited line anchors were re-verified against the actual revision files in this pass: `cmd/inspect.go` L67–L72 (flag), L182–L219 (`listContainers`), L222–L273 (`logicalNodeContainers`), `cmd/options.go` L417 (`Containers bool`), `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` L64–L76, `docs/manual/kinds/srl.md` L473, and `docs/rn/0.80.md` L250.
- Minor formatting nit: the added line `docs/cmd/inspect/index.md` L72 carries a trailing space after "topology node."; there is no markdownlint enforcement in CI (checked `.github/workflows/cicd.yml`), so it is recorded here rather than raised as a finding.
- `docs/rn/` has no changes in this PR; the behavior change (default view hides tool containers and internal containers; `--all` no longer lists internals) is user-visible and may warrant an entry in the next unreleased release note once one exists.
- Edge cases judged acceptable: stale non-CPM components are filtered from the logical view (intended grouping); a holder without its node container yields no row, matching base behavior; internal containers without `RootNodeName` (for example the tailscale proxy) are hidden rather than promoted to logical nodes, which matches the `key.node == ""` guard in the implementation.
